title: SDK Adoption Barrier Catalog & Triage Playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We receive a high volume of SDK/client library requests from enterprise customers and partners that vary across language support, auth patterns (token rotation, SSO), and streaming ergonomics. There is no repeatable intake cadence or scoring rubric, which causes inconsistent prioritization, long lead times, and missed signals for Dedicated/Private deployment requirements.

Goal: Create a repeatable playbook that catalogs common adoption barriers, defines a compact triage rubric (customer impact, engineering effort, compliance risk, strategic alignment), and prescribes concrete actions (shallow vs deep investment paths) to route requests to: quick fixes, SDK backlog, Dedicated workstream, or security/compliance track. This ticket produces the canonical playbook and an intake checklist template for Solutions/CS/SE teams.
triage_rubric: Customer Impact (0-5): number of customers affected and revenue/renewal risk
Effort (0-5): engineering hours estimate including infra, docs, QA
Security/Compliance Risk (0-5): need for KMS/HSM, SSO, data residency
Strategic Fit (0-5): aligns to SDK consolidation, Dedicated growth, or PLG funnels
Operational Complexity (0-5): maintenance burden (support, platform changes)
Total score guidance: 0-7 = Low, 8-14 = Medium, 15-25 = High priority
scoring_matrix: Quick fix path: Total <= 7 and Effort <= 2 -> schedule as a docs/adapter PR or example-client in next sprint
Medium path: Total 8-14 -> include in quarterly SDK milestone, require design + 2-sprint engineering slot
High path: Total >= 15 or Security/Compliance >=4 -> escalate to Dedicated/Private product lead, open EPIC with ENG and Security

Streaming ergonomics override: any request where streaming UX materially changes API semantics (server push, reconnect logic) should be evaluated with ENG-runtime and given minimum medium priority regardless of score
examples_sample_requests: Customer A (F500 fintech) requests a Java SDK that supports OIDC SSO with rotating short-lived tokens, plus audit logging to their SIEM. Preliminary asks: token refresh hook, session binding, and client-side telemetry headers.
Partner B (analytics startup) asks for a lightweight Go streaming client that exposes partial-result callbacks and backpressure hooks for bounded-latency pipelines.
Customer C (healthcare platform) requests an on-prem Python SDK variant that compiles against their internal TLS stack and supports HSM-backed key wrapping for encryption-at-rest.
Internal request: Solutions Engineering asks for a Node.js example adapter that demonstrates token rotation and retry best practices for streaming connections (used in three active pilots).
decisions: Adopt a single triage rubric (fields above) for Solutions/CS intake to produce a numeric score and recommended path.
Implement a lightweight intake form (Confluence template + linear shortcut) that surfaces required artifacts: customer use case, expected QPS, data class, desired SLA, PoC link if available.
Streaming ergonomics require a cross-team review with ENG-runtime and SDK owners before being deprioritized; treat streaming changes as higher risk to client ergonomics.

For enterprise-auth work (SSO/token rotation/HSM), create a template security checklist and require Security review before engineering kickoff. These requests default to High priority if compliance >3.
action_items: Draft Confluence intake template and share with SE + CS by 2025-03-14 (OWNER: Maya)
Build triage scoring sheet (Google Sheet) and integrate into weekly PM triage cadence (OWNER: Owen)
Pilot the rubric on last 8 SDK requests and capture historical scores to validate thresholds (OWNER: PM team)
Create a lightweight Node + Go example showing streaming backpressure + token refresh and ship as 'sdk-examples/streaming-interop' repo (OWNER: ENG - SDK team, dependency: ENG-4021)
Coordinate with Security to produce the auth/HSM checklist and expected timelines for compliance-required items (OWNER: Security Team)
Add a 'triage outcome' field to internal request tracker and notify requestor within 3 business days with next steps (OWNER: PM Ops)
Schedule a 30-minute sync with Runtime leads to align on streaming semantics and template handshake API shape (OWNER: Owen, target 2025-03-20)
Identify two existing SDKs to standardize token refresh hooks and document an official pattern (OWNER: SDK Maintainers)
If score >= 15, create a parent EPIC and assign ENG triage owner within 5 business days

2025-03-12 Owen: Draft rubric posted to shared sheet. Need ENG to validate 'Effort' buckets (small 1-8h, medium 1-2w, large >2w). Asked SDK owners to review.
2025-03-14 Elena (Security): Flagged that any HSM/KMS integration requires an information-security questionnaire and may add 4-6 week lead time. Will attach checklist to intake template.
2025-03-16 Raj (SDK lead): Agreed on streaming override. Suggested adding a 'reconnect semantics' subfield to intake so we know whether server-initiated messages are expected.
2025-03-18 Owen: Updated playbook with intake template link and assigned first pilot cohort (Customer A, Partner B). Next: run scoring workshop 2025-03-20 with ENG-runtime + SDK owners.
notes: This playbook should be revisited after two sprints and after the pilot to refine effort bands and streaming evaluation criteria. Keep the intake form intentionally short (max 8 fields) to reduce friction.
